title: The Rise of Low Precision Floating Point
abstract: arXiv:2611.00301v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Floating point computing has dominated scientific computations since the 1950s because of its versatile ability to approximate real numbers with both sufficiently high precision and sufficiently great range. Since 1985, two specific formats have become standard across the industry, one with 32 bits which is adequate for many purposes and one with 64 bits which allows numbers with both much higher precision and much greater range for applications where these are needed. However, during the past decade, deep learning has come to dominate computation, and narrower floating point formats with lower precision and reduced range have steadily become more common. In this article we discuss this phenomenon, why it is happening, how various 16-bit, 8-bit and even 4-bit floating point formats have been developed, and efforts to standardize these formats.

translated_abstract: 自20世纪50年代以来，浮点计算一直主导着科学计算，因为它具有以足够高的精度和足够大的取值范围来逼近实数的多功能能力。自1985年以来，两种特定格式已成为整个行业的标准：一种是32位格式，足以满足许多用途；另一种是64位格式，可为需要更高精度和更大范围的应用提供支持。然而，在过去十年中，深度学习逐渐主导了计算领域，精度更低、范围更小的窄位浮点格式也日益普及。本文讨论了这一现象，探讨了其发生的原因，介绍了各种16位、8位甚至4位浮点格式是如何发展起来的，以及为这些格式制定标准所做的努力。
tldr: 本文探讨了深度学习的兴起如何推动16位、8位乃至4位等低精度浮点格式的发展及其标准化进程。
en_tdlr: This paper discusses how the rise of deep learning has driven the development and standardization efforts of low-precision floating point formats, including 16-bit, 8-bit, and even 4-bit formats.
